# dutype

> Parallel disk usage analyzer that breaks a directory down by kind: file types (video, PDF, archives, ML models, data, code, ...) and special directories (node_modules, Python envs, .git, build output, package caches, ML caches). Interactive TUI for humans; JSON output and an MCP server for scripts and LLM agents. Written in Rust.

Agent usage: always pass `--json` or `--report`; plain `dutype PATH` opens an interactive TUI.

Version contract: this `main`-branch document describes a matching source build, not the current published v0.1.4 package. For the package, use `npx -y dutype@0.1.4 --json PATH` with the [v0.1.4 skill](https://github.com/william1010121/dutype/blob/v0.1.4/skills/dutype/SKILL.md) and [v0.1.4 README](https://github.com/william1010121/dutype/blob/v0.1.4/README.md). Use the directly linked tagged skill, not the older skill-download snippet in the tagged README, which points to `main`. Do not assume the options or JSON fields below exist in that release: `--include-files`, MCP pagination/cursors, category `matched_items`/`items_truncated`, and `accounting.measurement_basis`/`hardlink_deduplication` were added later. Inspect CLI help, MCP tool schemas, and returned payloads; the version string alone may not distinguish development builds. Update package and documentation pins together for future releases.

- `dutype --json PATH`: totals, per-category shares, biggest children, biggest special dirs (cleanup candidates), biggest files. Paths are absolute, sizes follow `accounting.measurement_basis`: `allocated` on Unix (like `du`), `logical` on non-Unix including Windows (file lengths), plus a human string (`size`). `accounting.hardlink_deduplication` is `count-once` on Unix, `unsupported` elsewhere (linked paths count separately). These describe native scan policy/capability, not observed duplicates. `accounting.size="du-allocated"` is a legacy, non-authoritative label. Caches assume same-platform reuse; they have no producer-platform tag and are not portable snapshots.
- Shared blocks (APFS clones on macOS, hard links), with `--clones` (opt-in, slower; without it `freeable_min_bytes` is null on macOS and `accounting.clone_detection` is `off`; it is also null on Linux reflink filesystems, with `--cross-fs` and on Windows): `freeable_min_bytes` is a lower-bound estimate under the scan accounting model (not additive; quote with `accounting.caveats`, never as guaranteed immediately available space), `dedup_bytes` counts each clone family once (additive), `clone_shared_bytes = size_bytes - dedup_bytes`, `accounting` says whether clones were detected and what is not considered (snapshots, partial clones). Without `--clones`, hard-linked files never count in `freeable_min_bytes`; with it, they count where all their links are inside. `--size-mode dedup` ranks lists by `dedup_bytes`.
- `dutype --json --category NAME PATH`: largest items of one category, e.g. `node_modules`, `Python env`, `Build output`, `Video`, `PDF`. Directory categories return directories, file categories return files. `matched_items` counts matches in the scanned/cached snapshot before the limit; a matching directory counts once and prunes descendants. `items_truncated` means `matched_items > items.length`, not scan incompleteness. `unreadable` is scan-wide; unknown entries are not inferred as matches. Text totals cover only displayed items.
- `dutype --json --private PATH` (macOS/APFS): files that are partial clones get `private_bytes`, the scan-time APFS attribute for bytes not retained by clones or snapshots that actual file deletion would release (never summed into folders). This is not a guaranteed future available-space delta: open references can delay deletion and cached values can be stale. `accounting.private` says whether they were collected. Opt-in; implies `--clones`.
- `dutype --top N`: list lengths (default 20). `--cross-fs`: descend into other mounts.
- `dutype --json --clones PATH`: detect shared blocks (slower): APFS clones on macOS; on Linux btrfs / XFS / bcachefs, shared extents (one FIEMAP ioctl per file), so `dedup_bytes` counts reflinked copies and snapshot-shared data once, like `btrfs filesystem du`'s "Set shared", and `freeable_min_bytes` never includes shared extents. Without it `freeable_min_bytes` is null on macOS and those filesystems. `accounting.clone_detection` says what was detected (`fiemap`, `fiemap-partial`, `apfs-full`, `apfs-partial`, `unsupported` or `off`).
- `--include-files` with `--category` and `--report` or `--json` (MCP `find_by_category`: `include_files: true`, default false) adds directly matching files to mixed directory/file categories. Both scanned category and direct filename classification must match; final extension overrides and Other's fallback apply. Matching directories still prune descendants even below top-N. The root is excluded, but explicit matching files below an excluded special root can appear; arbitrary inherited files cannot. Pure-category matches, default payloads, TUI and scan accounting stay unchanged. True is echoed in category JSON; inventory totals need not equal category summary totals. Not accepted with CLI `--mcp`/`--dump-config` or on MCP `disk_usage`.
- `dutype --dump-config`: every category and its rules (TOML). Users extend them in `~/.config/dutype/config.toml`.
- `dutype --mcp`: MCP server on stdio with read-only tools `disk_usage(path, top?, cross_fs?, refresh?, clones?, size_mode?, private?)` and `find_by_category(path, category, top?, cross_fs?, refresh?, clones?, size_mode?, private?, include_files?, paginate?, cursor?)` (`?` marks optional arguments; same fields as `--json`).
- With `dutype --mcp --cache`, `refresh: true` replaces only the session's in-memory snapshot; MCP never writes or replaces the CLI's disk cache. A CLI run with `--refresh` updates the disk snapshot used by future sessions.

- Category pagination is opt-in (`paginate: true`) with `--mcp --cache` and no server-wide `--refresh`. Follow `pagination.next_cursor` with the returned absolute path and same effective category/options, including `include_files`; changing that boolean rejects the cursor even for pure categories. `top` may change. Stop on `has_more: false`, not `items_truncated`. Pages describe one retained completed scan, not atomic/live filesystem truth. Refresh/capability replacement or process restart returns `stale_cursor` / `restart_required: true`; restart without a cursor. No per-cursor registry, old-tree pinning or disk writes; at most 500 candidates and two tree walks per page. Legacy calls are unchanged.
